result.question: For our transformer fleet planning, take the known failure modes for a transformer and tell me which of them we can actually watch on Transformer 1 at site MAIN with the channels it reports today. For each failure mode, list the two or three most diagnostic sensors among hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene, co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen, dbds, dielectric_rigidity, interfacial_v, oti, oti_a, oti_t, ati, il1, il2, il3 and inut. Then mark each mode as 'well covered', 'partially covered' or 'blind', based on whether those sensors have data in the available window. Only list sensors that genuinely discriminate that mode, not ones that just correlate generally. If a mode's key sensor exists but has no values in the window, count the mode as blind rather than covered, and suggest which offline test or extra sample would close the gap.
result.answer:
**Transformer 1 @ MAIN — failure-mode observability**

Data window: 5 daily records, 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19. All 20 sensors you named have 5 non-null numeric values across that window, so nothing is technically "blind" — but note the window is short (5 samples) and ~2.5 years old, so trend-based diagnostics are weak.

| # | Failure mode | Most diagnostic sensors (from your list) | Why they discriminate | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Partial Discharge in Oil | hydrogen, methane, acetylene | H₂-dominant with CH₄/H₂ < 0.1 and C₂H₂ ≈ 0 (IEC 60599 PD signature; acetylene absence separates it from arcing) | **Well covered** |
| 2 | Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating (T1/T2, <700 °C) | ethylene, ethane, oti | C₂H₄/C₂H₆ ratio sets the temperature band (ethane-dominant <300 °C, ethylene rising 300–700 °C); OTI confirms bulk-oil heating | **Well covered** |
| 3 | Thermal Fault — Core/Winding (T3, >700 °C) | ethylene, acetylene, il1/il2/il3 | Ethylene-dominant (C₂H₄/C₂H₆ > 4) with only trace C₂H₂ distinguishes hot-metal from arcing; phase-current imbalance localises a winding/circulating-current source | **Well covered** |
| 4 | Low-Energy Arcing (D1) | acetylene, hydrogen | C₂H₂/C₂H₄ > 1 with high H₂ — acetylene is the only gas essentially unique to arcing | **Well covered** |
| 5 | High-Energy Arcing (D2) | acetylene, ethylene, oti_t | C₂H₂/C₂H₄ 0.6–2.5 with C₂H₄/C₂H₆ > 2 (energy higher than D1); trip flag captures the event | **Well covered** |
| 6 | Tap Changer Mechanical Wear | acetylene, ethylene, il1/il2/il3 | Only indirect: OLTC contact coking/arcing leaks a D2-like C₂H₂+C₂H₄ pattern into main-tank oil, and current steps at tap events; none of the listed channels measure the mechanism itself | **Partially covered** — close the gap with an OLTC-compartment DGA sample, dynamic resistance measurement (DRM), and drive-motor current/torque + contact-timing test |
| 7 | Oil Contamination / Moisture Ingress | dielectric_rigidity, oxygen, nitrogen | Breakdown voltage collapses with water/particles; O₂ rise and O₂/N₂ ratio indicate seal breach / air ingress | **Well covered** (water_content is also on the asset with data, outside your list) |
| 8 | Cellulose Insulation Ageing | co2, co | CO₂/CO ratio (3–10 normal, >10 oxidative ageing, <3 paper overheating) is the only online cellulose-specific indicator | **Well covered** — a furan (2-FAL) sample or DP test is still needed to quantify remaining life |
| 9 | Oil Dielectric Degradation | interfacial_v, dbds, dielectric_rigidity | IFT drop = oxidation/polar by-products; DBDS depletion = corrosive-sulphur activity (Cu₂S risk); dielectric strength is the functional consequence | **Well covered** — add offline acidity (neutralization number) and Cu₂S/CCD test |

**Summary:** 8 of 9 modes well covered, 1 (Tap Changer Mechanical Wear) partially covered, 0 blind. The main fleet-planning gap is OLTC health — it needs its own compartment sampling/DRM rather than main-tank channels. Also worth flagging: the current window shows very high H₂/CH₄/C₂H₄ (≈2,900 / 7,300 / 16,600 ppm) with oti_a and oti_t set, so a fresh DGA sample should be pulled before relying on this data for planning.
